core_principles.text: Changing the hand formation from a supinated to a neutral grip alters the biomechanics of the arm during elbow flexion.
During both neutral and supinated bicep curls, the biceps brachii is positioned optimally to perform elbow flexion efficiently.
Performing a bicep curl with a pronated grip increases the activation of the brachioradialis because the biceps brachii is placed at a biomechanical disadvantage.

specific_findings.text: In a study of 5 male participants (Age 23.6 ± 1.1 yrs), the mean torque during the initial 40 degrees of elbow flexion was 34.22 ± 6.14 N*m for a neutral grip and 33.84 ± 7.56 N*m for a supinated grip, showing no statistically significant difference (p > .05).
The mean power during the initial 40 degrees of elbow flexion was measured at 49.35 ± 8.61 watts for a neutral grip and 53.04 ± 14.70 watts for a supinated grip.
The brachioradialis acts primarily as a synergist muscle during neutral and supinated elbow flexion at heavy loads.

consequences.text: Using a pronated hand position puts the biceps brachii at a biomechanical disadvantage during elbow flexion, which significantly increases the workload and muscle activity required from the brachioradialis.

source: data\bicep-curl\THE COMPARISON OF MUSCLE ACTIVATION AND PERFORMANCE IN A NEUTRAL AND SUPINATED GRIP BICEP CURL.pdf [part 1/2]

core_principles.text: There is no significant difference in overall muscle activity and performance between a neutral grip and a supinated grip bicep curl.
During the first 40 degrees of elbow flexion, both neutral and supinated grips produce similar average torque and power.

specific_findings.text: The mean value for power during the initial 40 degrees of elbow flexion was 49.35 ± 8.61 watts during a neutral grip bicep curl and 53.04 ± 14.70 watts during a supinated bicep curl.
The mean value for MVC% for the brachioradialis during the first 40 degrees of elbow flexion was 67.70 ± 9.08% during a neutral grip bicep curl and 63.84 ± 8.19% during a supinated bicep curl.
The mean value for the average EMG activity for the brachioradialis was 565.17 ± 163.80 μvolts during a neutral grip bicep curl and 541.80 ± 165.46 μvolts during a supinated bicep curl.
The mean value for average torque during the first 40 degrees of elbow flexion was 34.22 ± 6.14 N*m during a neutral grip bicep curl and 33.84 ± 7.56 N*m during a supinated grip bicep curl.

source: data\bicep-curl\THE COMPARISON OF MUSCLE ACTIVATION AND PERFORMANCE IN A NEUTRAL AND SUPINATED GRIP BICEP CURL.pdf [part 2/2]
